# Bring back PII input guardrail as a LangGraph middleware node

<!-- AT-A-GLANCE:BEGIN -->
<!-- Auto-generated by render-plan-on-write.sh; do not hand-edit. -->
<!-- AT-A-GLANCE:END -->

## 1. Motivation

User PII (email, credit-card numbers) entered in the agent chat currently reaches the LLM provider, the LangGraph checkpointer, and the background memory extractor unchanged. A prior implementation (`feat/min-62-pii-guardrail`, commits `a153706` / `7cacf1a`) fixed this but is not present on the current HEAD. We need to bring it back as a pre-model guardrail — the LangGraph idiomatic equivalent of middleware — so the model never sees sensitive input, while keeping names/phone untouched so MIN-53 personalization still works.

## 2. Non-goals

- No encryption at rest for bookings (out of scope; separate data-model task).
- No output redaction of the assistant's replies (input-only guardrail).
- No new dependency; reuse stdlib + LangChain already in `.venv`.
- No migration; no DB schema change.
- Do not redact names or phone numbers — those are required by the personalization flow and booking tools respectively.

## 3. Success Criteria

- Any user message containing email or credit-card numbers has those values redacted/masked before any LLM call.
- The redacted form is what gets persisted to the checkpointer and read by the memory extractor.
- Existing agent tests keep passing.
- New tests cover: email redaction, card masking (including glued expiry/non-standard lengths), guardrail node in-place replacement, graph end-to-end, and router persistence.

## 4. Tasks

### Task 1.1 — Restore the guardrail module (wave 1)

- **Files:** `apps/api/app/agents/guardrails.py`, `apps/api/tests/agents/test_pii_redaction.py`
- **Action:** Create `apps/api/app/agents/guardrails.py` with a pure `redact_pii(text)` function plus a `pii_guardrail_node(state)` LangGraph node. Scope: email → `[REDACTED_EMAIL]`; credit card (13–19 digits, Luhn window search) → `****-****-****-<last4>`. The node finds the latest `HumanMessage`, redacts its string content, and returns a replacement message with the **same id** so `add_messages` overwrites in place. Copy the hardened logic from commit `7cacf1a` verbatim. Then add `tests/agents/test_pii_redaction.py` with unit tests for `redact_pii` (email, 16-digit card, 15-digit Amex, card glued to expiry, dot/newline separators, no-PII passthrough) and for `pii_guardrail_node` (in-place id preservation, no-op when clean).
- **Verify:** `cd apps/api && ../../.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/agents/test_pii_redaction.py -x`
- **Done:** Guardrail module exists, all new unit tests pass.

Add an end-to-end test in `tests/agents/test_graph.py` (or extend `test_pii_redaction.py`) that invokes the compiled graph with a fake LLM capturing input messages and asserts email/card are not present in the captured model input.

## 5. Risks

- **Personalization regression:** The guardrail intentionally leaves names untouched, matching the old scope. If a future requirement expands PII redaction to names, MIN-53 memory extraction must be redesigned.
- **False positives:** The Luhn-window card detector masks any 13–19 digit run that contains a valid Luhn window. This is acceptable for user chat (order numbers are rare in travel chat) and matches the previously accepted behavior.
- **Multimodal messages:** Only string `content` is redacted. Image/audio content blocks pass through unchanged (no PII in current product scope).
- **Phone numbers:** Left untouched because booking tools need the raw phone and the old scope excluded them.
